source.title: Sorting out Lipschitz function approximation
source.authors: Cem Anil; James Lucas; R. Grosse

record.tranche_reason: The study applies dropout and compares test error with a no-dropout baseline on MNIST classifiers, directly measuring the outcome named by V6.
record.gate_note: Dropout results in Tables 4 and 5 are included. Other classifier comparisons do not test the claim versions; cited findings are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: Tables 4 and 5 directly compare MNIST test error with and without dropout in fully connected and convolutional classifiers, testing V6 with the same intervention and outcome.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors identify gradient norm preservation as important for expressive Lipschitz networks, report improved Wasserstein estimates and adversarial robustness with GroupSort, and describe dropout as the most effective regularizer in their limited-data experiment overall. That description does not imply dropout wins in every activation/data-size cell; Table 5 nevertheless shows dropout lowers test error against the unregularized baseline in every reported cell.
record.recipe_differences: Applies dropout and compares with unregularized baselines, but the study focuses on Lipschitz-constrained network expressivity and classification rather than systematically studying dropout generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Dropout outcomes vary by activation and training-data size.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 97, 2019
record.problems: Dropout comparisons are limited to MNIST classifiers; the limited-data table reports results by activation and data size, with mixed outcomes. No uncertainty estimates are stated for these test-error comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Controlled comparisons of convolutional and fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.

Excessive dropout causing underfitting; dropout-rate dependence; removing dropout and weight decay together under data augmentation. Convolutional dropout comparisons are tested in Table 5, contrary to the record's untested-parts entry.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness ranking generalization gaps against competing measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States describe the direction and strength of dropout's test-error reduction; the small-data verdict separately addresses V6's explicit exception. No uncertainty or significance estimates accompany Tables 4–5, and dropout rates are not specified in the supplied text. The study is not an original source for V6.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the effect of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning or training recipes.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Convolutional dropout comparisons and removing dropout together with weight decay under data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
